analysis.title: Americas Real Estate: REITs: MAA/INVH: Both Miss on New Lease, and MAA Lowers Outlook
key_insights: INVH and MAA reported mixed 3Q26 results. The key divergence was on guidance: INVH raised FY26 Core FFO and same-store NOI guidance slightly, while MAA lowered FY26 same-store revenue, same-store NOI and Core FFO guidance.

INVH's guidance increase was driven by lower expenses, not stronger topline growth. FY26 same-store expense growth guidance midpoint fell to 3.20% from 3.5%, while the same-store revenue midpoint stayed at 1.9%.
INVH new lease rent growth was -0.2% in 3Q26, below consensus of +0.3%. GS had warned of a new lease miss in its 3Q26 preview, citing the BAML update and weak scraping data.
MAA new lease rates were -6.0%, about 40 bps below GSe and 80 bps below consensus. Blended rates were +0.4%, 10 bps below GSe and 50 bps below consensus.

MAA management said October new lease pricing improved from September and blends accelerated more than 100 bps YoY. GS calls this disappointing against expectations of a 226 bps YoY blends improvement in 4Q26.
GS expects both stocks to underperform the next day, with MAA under the most pressure because of the cuts to same-store and FFO guidance, weaker 3Q26 new lease rates and the October blends update.

INVH repurchased about $250mn of shares (8.9mn shares) in 3Q, $400mn since 2Q26, including $300mn since the BAML update as of Sept 4. It funded this with $245mn of proceeds from net dispositions of 442 homes.

MAA bought back $50mn of shares at an average $126.72 in 3Q, in line with GSe of $50mn. It acquired a Northern Virginia land parcel for a 306-unit development and sold its 35%-owned Washington, D.C. JV asset for about $147mn.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps its Buy and $33 12-month target, based on a 15.9x Q5-Q8 FFO multiple. It expects a modestly negative share reaction because the guidance raise was expense-driven and new lease rates missed consensus, partly offset by buybacks and better renewals.

GS keeps its Neutral and $125 12-month target, based on a 14.7x Q5-Q8 FFO multiple. It expects the stock to underperform after the cuts to FY26 Core FFO and same-store guidance, weak new lease spreads and the October blends update.

sector_views.rationale: 3Q26 new lease pricing was weak at both INVH and MAA. Guidance moved up at INVH only on lower expenses and down at MAA on weaker revenue.

earnings_insights: INVH 3Q26 Core FFO reported $0.48 per share vs GSe $0.49 and consensus $0.48. FFO (diluted) was $0.36 vs GSe $0.47 and consensus $0.46.
INVH 3Q26 same-store revenue +1.6% YoY vs GSe 1.9% and consensus 2.1%. Same-store expense +2.5% vs GSe 1.9% and consensus 2.9%. Same-store NOI +1.1% vs GSe 1.8% and consensus 1.7%.
INVH 3Q26 new/renewal/blended rent growth was -0.2%/+4.3%/+3.0%, versus GSe -0.4%/4.2%/2.8% and consensus +0.3%/3.8%/3.0%. Occupancy was 96.4% vs GSe 96.5%.

INVH FY26 Core FFO guidance raised to $1.94-$1.98 ($1.96 midpoint, up $0.01), vs GSe $1.98 and consensus $1.96. Same-store revenue midpoint unchanged at 1.9%, expense growth midpoint 3.20% vs 3.5% prior, same-store NOI midpoint 1.2% vs 1.15% prior.
MAA 3Q26 Core FFO reported $2.10 per share vs GSe $2.08 (about 1% above GS) and consensus $2.10. FFO (diluted) was $2.11 vs GSe $2.08.
MAA 3Q26 same-store revenue -0.4% YoY vs GSe -0.5% and consensus 0.0%. Same-store expense +2.0% vs GSe 1.5% and consensus 2.3%. Same-store NOI -1.8% vs GSe -1.8% and consensus -1.5%.
MAA 3Q26 new/renewal/blended lease rates were -6.0%/+5.3%/+0.4%. Occupancy was 95.3%.

MAA lowered FY26 same-store NOI growth guidance to -1.70% to -0.80% (-1.25% midpoint) from a -0.90% midpoint. Same-store revenue guidance is -0.40% to -0.10% (-0.25% midpoint) vs a prior +0.10% midpoint. Expense growth guidance is 1.15%-1.65% (1.40% midpoint) vs a prior 1.75%.
MAA FY26 Core FFO guidance lowered to $8.43-$8.55 ($8.49 midpoint) from a prior $8.53 midpoint, vs GSe $8.43 and consensus $8.49. 4Q26 Core FFO guidance is $2.18 vs GSe $2.14 and consensus $2.18.
risk_factors: INVH downside risks: greater-than-expected supply pressure, weaker demand, lower acquisition yields, higher hurricane and natural disaster costs, higher property operating expense growth, and the short-term interest rate path.
MAA upside and downside risks: more or less supply pressure, weaker or stronger demand, acquisition and development yields above or below underwriting, and high or low property expenses.
vol_and_positioning: INVH has repurchased $400mn of shares since 2Q26, including $300mn since the BAML update as of Sept 4, which GS cites as a partial offset to the weak new lease print.
cross_bank_references: GS cites 'the BAML update' on INVH as a basis for expecting a new lease miss.
